svg.title: Nightly Mode -- AI grading deferred to a per-submission rerun

g.text: Nightly Mode -- AI grading deferred to a per-submission rerun
Phase 1: on submission -- tests only, mark the work
grading_mode is NIGHTLY, so the AI component
is not invoked. Targets whose tests passed are
marked ai_needed = false and cost nothing
further. The ai_needed = true rows are what
Phase 2: nightly -- trigger a rerun per submission
Rerun is per submission, so the trigger job
iterates only submissions that actually need
work. It never touches an already-graded one.
This is still the one fragile step in the
design: Gradescope has no public API, so
locating a submission and clicking its rerun
button is UI automation and will break when
they reskin. Keep every selector in one file.
Consider throttling the loop. A term's worth
of submissions clicked as fast as Playwright
can manage looks like abuse from the outside.
Phase 3: the rerun -- AI grading for marked targets
query and before any LLM call. Reruns happen
for reasons other than our nightly job: an
instructor debugging the autograder, a TA
re-running a flaky test. None of those
Set only when no task is still NEEDED. On
partial failure it stays NULL, so tomorrow's
trigger picks the submission up and retries
just the failed targets. Once set it is never
cleared, and the trigger stops selecting this
Rules to ratify before A and C write two
1. A failed task stays NEEDED and increments
attempt_count. The next night retries it
2. LLM calls retry with backoff on 429 and 5xx
3. If the trigger cannot find or click a
submission's rerun button, record it on
trigger_run and surface it to the
instructor. A silent trigger failure looks
